assessments.reasoning: The OSI documentary record's three crosswalk ranges agree with the frozen bindings and directly provide the canonical link, title and MIT display label. The lowercase path limits literal URL comparison while the explicit identifier supports the OSI side of the correspondence.

The acquisition URL pins the SPDX project's MIT detail file to the specified commit. The 8433-byte response reports SHA-256 0c2b3c87a154a4aaac6bc6a735dd454dc29d9a78c23a85deedb080e0c65de1f8. All four reported ranges agree with the bindings for name, licenseId, crossRef and seeAlso. The distinct URL-level match values qualify what each reference can establish.

challenge.method: Compared the paths case-sensitively, checked both URL lists, and inspected each crossRef object's own match and liveness metadata.
challenge.results: OSI ends its path with lowercase mit and SPDX uses uppercase MIT. SPDX records match as the string N/A for OSI and false for the separate X.Org COPYING reference. Both entries are marked live and valid at the recorded September 16 timestamp. Those fields do not show a redirect or an affirmative text match. The X.Org result belongs to its own URL and leaves the OSI label correspondence intact.

limitations: The 3.29.0 release designation comes from the specified release-to-commit binding. The detail file identifies its content at the pinned commit and contains no release-tag history.
These acquisitions supply no live redirect test, historical comparison, blanket equivalence, byte-identity finding, template-match determination or project-specific license identification.
